text: 5 2021 Weekly Offering Envelopes The boxes of 2021 weekly offering envelopes have arrived. You may pick your box up on the round table in the Sanctuary. - The boxes will be in alphabetical order to ease your selection. Please note - there are several number changes to conform with the different ways many are now contributing. Those who are contributing on-line or through Bank Billpay will be not be receiving envelopes. However, I would ask two things: 1. If you did not receive a box of envelopes and would like one, please let Terry Hambel know. 2. If you received a box and will not need it for 2021, also let Terry know. As always, if you have any questions, you can contact Terry by leaving a message at 910-769-1761 or emailing tmurtha2@aol.com. Thank you all. Medicare Open Enrollment: October 15 - December 7, 2020 All Medicare beneficiaries are encouraged to examine their prescription drug coverage each year, as policies and prices change. In addition, the medication needs of an individual can change from year to year. This year some plans will be offering a Senior's Savings Model where a thirty-day supply of insulin vials and pen injections will cost a maximum of \$35. You may want to see if your current plan offers this model. You may find that changing Prescription Drug plans saves you money. During Open Enrollment, the New Hanover County Senior Resource Center will have SHIP volunteers available to provide one-on-one counseling by phone only. Due to the pandemic and limited availability, please call the appointment line at 910-798-6442. They will give you any further information that you may need. President's Letter June 2019 Kure Memorial Lutheran Church Part II (Written by The Federal Point Historical Society's President: Elaine Henson) Kure Memorial Chapel was "Serving the Savior by the Sea" and almost five years old when members and Kure Beach residents were invited to a meeting on August 21, 1951 to discuss its future. Those attending voted that the Chapel would become Kure Memorial Evangelical Church and affiliated with North Carolina Synod of the United Lutheran Church of America. That organizational meeting marks the birthday of Kure Memorial Evangelical Lutheran Church. Eighteen adults were present at that meeting including Mrs. Laura Kure Williford, Miss Anne Kure, Margaret and Robert Ford, Bessie and Fred Schenk, Lawrence C. Kure, Oscar and Anna Lee Wren, Isabell and Merritt Foushee, Betty Kure (Mrs. A. E. Sr.) and Jean Gore (later Jean Kure, Mrs. A. E. Jr.). The group adopted a constitution and elected the following church council members: Lawrence C. Kure, Vice Chairman, Margaret Ford, Secretary, Anne Kure, Treasurer and W. E. Williford, Sunday School Superintendent and Council Members Robert Ford, Oscar Wrenn, Merritt Foushee and Fred Schenk. The council decided to leave the charter membership open until one month after the arrival of a full time Pastor. On Sunday evening, August 26, 1951 the new church held a special service to mark the organization of Kure Memorial Evangelical Lutheran in the barracks church building. Celebrants were Rev. K.Y. Huddle of St. Matthews Lutheran, Rev. J. Frank Davis of St. Paul's Lutheran and seminarian Jack Martin. The congregation applied for membership in the North Carolina Synod on October 7, 1951. Rev. Huddle and Rev. Davis continued with Sunday evening services throughout the winter months. The first congregational meeting was held on January 9, 1952.
